questions.question: Sami and Mina receive a partially edentulous patient. Sami says: 'An implant is simple!' Mina asks him: 'Are you sure you know what a dental implant is?' What is a dental implant?
options: A titanium artificial root placed in the bone to replace a missing tooth
A crown placed on a devitalized natural tooth
A bridge bonded to adjacent teeth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The implant is an artificial titanium root that integrates with the bone (osseointegration) to support a prosthesis.' Sami, slightly annoyed, replies: 'I knew that, I just wanted to test you!'

questions.question: Sami, in a hurry, wants to place an implant without prior planning. Mina stops him: 'Sami, you must always plan!' Why is planning crucial in implantology?
options: To determine the ideal position, angle, and depth of the implant
To impress the patient with a scan
To increase the cost of treatment
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Rigorous planning with CBCT and surgical guides allows placing the implant in the ideal position.' Sami, slightly embarrassed, admits she is right.

questions.question: Mina shows Sami a CBCT and explains the concept of osseointegration. Sami asks: 'What exactly is that?' Mina replies:
options: The direct structural bond between living bone and the implant surface
The healing of the gum around the implant
The formation of new blood vessels
The growth of bone around the crown
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Osseointegration is the key to success in implantology, it's the functional union between bone and titanium.' Sami, fascinated, promises to learn more.

questions.question: Sami, confidently, tells Mina he will place an implant in 20 minutes. Mina asks him: 'But how do you choose the length of the implant?' Sami replies:
options: Based on the available bone height measured on the CBCT
Based solely on the tooth to be replaced
Taking the longest possible to be sure
Based on the color of the gum
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The available bone height is a determining factor, it must be measured precisely on the CBCT.' Sami, slightly unsettled, promises to check.

questions.question: Mina, analyzing an X-ray, says: 'Sami, there is insufficient bone density.' Sami asks: 'What does that mean?'
options: The bone does not have sufficient quality to support an implant
The bone is too hard to drill
The bone is too close to the nerve
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Bone density is a key factor, it influences the primary stability of the implant.' Sami, taking notes, asks how to improve this density.

questions.question: Sami asks Mina how to improve insufficient bone density. Mina replies:
options: By bone grafting or using wider implants
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Bone grafts allow rebuilding bone volume, and larger diameter implants can improve stability.' Sami, attentive, follows her advice.

questions.question: Sami, preparing a patient, asks Mina: 'What is primary stability?' Mina replies:
options: The immediate mechanical fixation of the implant in the bone after placement
The healing of the gum around the implant
The strength of the crown after 6 months
The formation of bone around the implant
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Primary stability is essential, it allows good osseointegration.' Sami, focused, seeks the best possible stability.

questions.question: Mina, while instrumenting, tells Sami: 'Be careful not to heat the bone during drilling!' Sami asks: 'Why?' Mina replies:
options: Heat can cause bone necrosis and compromise osseointegration
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Abundant irrigation is necessary to avoid thermal necrosis of the bone.' Sami, cautious, checks the irrigation well.

questions.question: Sami has placed an implant and asks Mina: 'How long should we wait before placing the crown?' Mina replies:
options: Generally 3 to 6 months, the time for osseointegration
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The delay varies depending on the case, but as a general rule, you must allow time for the bone to integrate with the implant.' Sami, taking notes, is more patient.

questions.question: Mina explains to Sami the concept of immediate loading. Sami asks: 'What is it?' Mina replies:
options: The placement of a provisional crown within 48 hours of implant placement
The placement of the implant without surgery
The placement of a definitive crown the same day
The absence of a crown on the implant
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Immediate loading is possible in selected cases, with excellent primary stability.' Sami, surprised, promises to look into it.

questions.question: Sami, seeing an implant with an incorrect angle, asks Mina: 'Should it be removed?' Mina replies:
options: Not necessarily, you can sometimes use an angled abutment
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Angled abutments can correct axis defects.' Sami, relieved, learns this trick.

questions.question: Mina places an implant in an aesthetic zone. Sami asks her: 'Why do you pay attention to the position?' Mina replies:
options: The position of the implant determines the aesthetics of the final crown
The position is not important for aesthetics
The position only matters for chewing
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The three-dimensional position of the implant is crucial for an optimal aesthetic result.' Sami, observing, admires her work.

questions.question: Sami, after placing an implant, asks Mina: 'What are the signs of a successful implant?' Mina replies:
options: No pain, no mobility, normal X-ray
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Success criteria include no pain, no mobility, and an X-ray without bone loss.' Sami, reassured, validates his work.

questions.question: Mina, examining a patient, tells Sami: 'There is bone loss around the implant.' Sami asks: 'What could that be?'
options: Peri-implantitis, an infection around the implant
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Peri-implantitis is a serious complication, it requires prompt management.' Sami, worried, asks how to treat it.

questions.question: Sami asks Mina how to treat peri-implantitis. Mina replies:
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Treatment is complex and often requires a surgical approach.' Sami, attentive, promises to train.

questions.question: Mina, planning a case, uses a surgical guide. Sami asks: 'What is it for?' Mina replies:
options: To guide drilling to place the implant in the ideal position
To increase the cost of treatment
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The surgical guide allows millimeter precision.' Sami, admiring, is interested in this technology.

questions.question: Sami, looking at an X-ray, asks Mina: 'How can you tell if the bone is sufficient for an implant?' Mina replies:
options: With a CBCT scan that gives a 3D view of the bone
With a photo of the patient
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'CBCT is the reference tool for 3D bone assessment.' Sami, taking notes, understands the importance of this imaging.

questions.question: Mina, preparing a case, tells Sami: 'We must protect the inferior alveolar nerve.' Sami asks: 'Why?'
options: To avoid nerve damage with neurological sequelae
To make the implant hold better
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The inferior alveolar nerve is at risk, a safety distance must be respected.' Sami, very attentive, is more cautious.

questions.question: Sami, looking at an X-ray, asks Mina: 'What does a safety distance of 2mm from the nerve mean?' Mina replies:
options: It is the minimum recommended distance to avoid damaging the nerve
It is the maximum permitted distance
It is the distance that allows better anchoring
It is the distance that speeds up healing
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A safety distance helps avoid complications.' Sami, cautious, always checks this distance.

questions.question: Mina, placing an implant, pays attention to the drilling angle. Sami asks her: 'Why is the angle so important?' Mina replies:
options: To follow the prosthetic axis and avoid complications
To make the implant more aesthetic
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A bad axis can compromise the entire prosthetic restoration.' Sami, attentive, follows her example.

questions.question: Sami, after an implantation, asks Mina: 'What are the recommended post-operative care instructions?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A well-followed post-operative protocol is essential to avoid complications.' Sami, conscientious, explains everything to the patient.

questions.question: Mina, reassessing a patient, tells Sami: 'The implant is well osseointegrated.' Sami asks: 'How do you know?'
options: No mobility, normal X-ray, asymptomatic patient
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Osseointegration is confirmed by the absence of mobility and a normal X-ray.' Sami, satisfied, validates the result.

questions.question: Sami asks Mina: 'What are the most common implant materials?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Titanium is the reference material thanks to its biocompatibility.' Sami, taking notes, expands his knowledge.

questions.question: Mina, explaining a case, tells Sami: 'There are contraindications to implantology.' Sami asks: 'Which ones?'
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Certain medical conditions can compromise the success of implants.' Sami, attentive, evaluates each patient.

questions.question: Mina finishes a surgery and tells Sami: 'Now we need to take care of the prosthesis.' Sami asks: 'What is the simplest prosthetic solution?'
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The single crown is the simplest and most common solution.' Sami, agreeing, prepares the impression.

questions.question: Sami, seeing the final result, tells Mina: 'It's beautiful!' Mina replies: 'It's the result of good planning and rigorous execution.' Sami, impressed, promises to be more meticulous in the future.
options: The aesthetic result depends on the initial planning
The aesthetic result does not depend on the surgeon
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Initial planning determines the final aesthetic result.' Sami, convinced, adopts this philosophy.
